trickyParts: The daemon must not import the envoy module in its production build (packages/daemon/internal/agentsecrets/contract_test.go states that invariant), so the generator writes a second file into the daemon's own package rather than the daemon importing contracts. Both outputs are checked by `bun run check:go`, and both CI paths-filters that reach that command name the new file — without the `envoy` filter the new generated file would be hand-editable with no job checking it.

Two fixtures were sized to the old cap and stopped testing what they were written for: the reader-tab guard in Unfurl.test.tsx (resized; isBareReferenceBody measured at 4.380 ms for three 31,998-character bodies of repeated schemes against its unchanged 2,000 ms budget, so it is linear at the new cap and no production change was needed) and the merge-withdrawal cut-to-fit fixture in ready_test.go (CI caught it; now derived from the constant).

The pathological-write premise in search_pathological_test.go said comments were too short to ladder. A full-cap `a_` comment is 32 KB of exactly the shape migration 0056 measured at 5 s before search_text bounded it, so the file now ladders comments at DispatchBodyMax/32, /4 and the cap, held by its existing growsLinearly bound. CI's `go test` is not verbose, so the rung times are not printed; the bound is asserted rather than eyeballed, and the test fails if a write stops being linear.

deviations: The plan's live proof commands (`bun run dispatch:local`, `bun run e2e`, the Go tests wanting a DSN) cannot run in a Legion worker pod: no Docker socket, no Postgres, no psql, and no C compiler to build pgvector for one. The architect confirmed CI as the production-like surface for every criterion and that each proof cites the run id, job, test, assertion and head. Nothing here claims a local run of those lanes.

The plan named no harness for AC2 and none existed. On the architect's instruction a new browser-suite row spawns the real `dispatch` command against the running Dispatch, so the criterion is proven in CI rather than by hand.

The deployment instruction requires a reader-facing Dispatch change to be proven by a browser test failing before the change and passing at the head; the plan did not name one. packages/dispatch/e2e/composer-body-cap.e2e.ts is that test, with the failing half run on branch `infra-45-composer-cap-base` (pull request #2098, run 39655782661) over commit 588363c261fb.

The plan's T8 table listed skills/dispatch/SKILL.md; a rewrite on main had already removed every body-cap number from it and from skills/dispatch/references/, so there was nothing to sweep there. Confirmed on main@origin.

`packages/dispatch/web/src/features/conversation/composer-references.test.ts` and the performance.now() millisecond budgets in both browser tests were left alone, as the plan's spec departure and the architect's ruling say: those budgets are the catastrophic-backtracking guard.
discoveredComplexity: A document's whole margin is bounded at 1 MiB, not only 256 KiB per record (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/growth.go, pmdoc.MaxDocumentBytes): about 32 full-length ASCII comments, or about 10 CJK ones, now fill it, after which every further comment or suggestion on that document is refused 413. Escalated; the architect accepted it with no work.

Embedding cost per comment rises up to sixteenfold: embed.maxInputChars is 32,000 runes, so a full-cap comment is now embedded whole, about 8,000 tokens against embedqueue's 200,000-token ceiling. Escalated; accepted with no work.

A 32,000-character agent turn is cut at AGENT_STREAM_LIMITS.partChars = 16,000 in the dashboard's Agent view. Delivery to the agent is unaffected, so AC3 still holds; only what a human watching that page sees is cut. Escalated; the architect ruled it outside this issue.
